```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

We explored using sampling with replacement to get a sense of both the total number of individuals of each size sampled at the different stations in the EBS. Essentially it would incorporate both the abundance information and length information in the same place. 
However, we don't necessarily need/want that information in the same model (depending on our questions).

For now lets explore length models without accounting for total catch

  st_as_sf(crs = 4326)

# xmin = 185 (-175), xmax = 202 (-155)

# crop

bs_base <- bs_map %>% 
  st_make_valid() %>% 
  st_intersection(st_as_sfc(bbox_360)) %>%
  st_shift_longitude() 

bs_utm <- bs_base %>%
  st_transform(crs = 32602) # Move to UTM Zone 2N

# 1. lng SDMtmb
```{r}
head(lngs)
# check for NAs
table(is.na(lngs$corrected_length)) # 17 true
table(is.na(lngs$eq_latitude))
table(is.na(lngs$eq_longitude))
table(is.na(lngs$haul_date))


lngs_utm <- lngs %>%
  # for now we'll remove the na lengths but ideally we'll fix this on the db side so it won't be a prblem
  filter(!(is.na(corrected_length))) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(haul_date),
         doy = yday(date),
         median_doy = median(doy),
         scale_doy = doy - median_doy,
         mean_doy = mean(doy),
         sd_doy = sd(doy),
         scale_doy2 = (doy - mean_doy)/sd_doy,
         scaled_median = (median_doy - mean_doy) / sd_doy) %>%
  arrange(station_id) %>%
  dplyr::select(c(sample_year, station_id, doy, scale_doy, scale_doy2, scaled_median, eq_latitude, eq_longitude, corrected_length)) %>%
  add_utm_columns(., ll_names = c("eq_longitude", "eq_latitude"),
                  ll_crs = 4326, utm_names = c("X", "Y"), 
                  units = "km") # uses crs 32602
  
# create mesh
mesh.lng <- make_mesh(lngs_utm, c("X", "Y"), n_knots = 75)
plot(mesh.lng)
```

# fit measured lengths

We have a couple options to how we fit this:
- we can use a gaussian 
- we can use a lognormal
- generalized gamma 
```{r}
fit.gaus <- sdmTMB(
  data = lngs_utm,
  # model formula
  corrected_length ~ 0 + s(scale_doy2) + as.factor(sample_year),
  # add mesh
  mesh = mesh.lng, 
  # we want to fit a spatiotemporal model with iid so we need to say which is the time category
  time = "sample_year", 
  # family important.... start with gaussian
  family = gaussian(),
  #family = lognormal(link = "log"), 
  spatial = "on",
  # each year independentally estimated
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  # we want ansiotropy because we want to assume that the decomposition of Matern distance isn't
  # necessarily the same EW as NS. Esp cause in the BS we have the shelf patterns that can drive 
  # species distributions
  anisotropy = TRUE
)

fit.logN <- sdmTMB(
  data = lngs_utm,
  # model formula
  corrected_length ~ 0 + s(scale_doy2) + as.factor(sample_year),
  # add mesh
  mesh = mesh.lng, 
  # we want to fit a spatiotemporal model with iid so we need to say which is the time category
  time = "sample_year", 
  # family important.... start with gaussian
  family = lognormal(link = "log"),
  spatial = "on",
  # each year independentally estimated
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  # we want ansiotropy because we want to assume that the decomposition of Matern distance isn't
  # necessarily the same EW as NS. Esp cause in the BS we have the shelf patterns that can drive 
  # species distributions
  anisotropy = TRUE
)

fit.gamma <- sdmTMB(
  data = lngs_utm,
  # model formula
  corrected_length ~ 0 + s(scale_doy2) + as.factor(sample_year),
  # add mesh
  mesh = mesh.lng, 
  # we want to fit a spatiotemporal model with iid so we need to say which is the time category
  time = "sample_year", 
  # family important.... start with gaussian
  family = gengamma(link = "log"),
  spatial = "on",
  # each year independentally estimated
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  # we want ansiotropy because we want to assume that the decomposition of Matern distance isn't
  # necessarily the same EW as NS. Esp cause in the BS we have the shelf patterns that can drive 
  # species distributions
  anisotropy = TRUE
)
```


Do they all converge appropriately?
```{r}
sanity(fit.gaus)
sanity(fit.logN)
sanity(fit.gamma)

# all converge appropriately

AIC(fit.gaus); AIC(fit.logN); AIC(fit.gamma)

# generalized gamma has the lowest AIC

# initial look at the random parameters, look similar (aside from the expected diff bc of log links)
tidy(fit.gaus, "ran_pars") # is the wild sd scaled doy bc its gaussian?
tidy(fit.logN, "ran_pars") 
tidy(fit.gamma, "ran_pars")
```

## model evalutions
```{r}
# model list:
# already removed nbs pcod because that model doesn't converge nice
model.list <- list(fit.gaus, fit.logN, fit.gamma)
names(model.list) <- c("fit.gaus", "fit.logN", "fit.gamma")
```

### gradient check
```{r}
check_gradient <- function(model) {
  if(any(model$gradients > 0.0005)){
    print(paste("model has too large of a gradient:", names(model)))
  } else {
    print("model passes gradient check")
  }
}

for(i in 1:length(model.list)) {
  print(names(model.list)[[i]])
  check_gradient(model.list[[i]])
}
```

### residual plots
this takes longer to run since i'm simulating 500 times to then extract dharma residuals.
```{r}
# create empty plot list
residual.plots <- list()
spatial.plots <- list()
residual.df <- list()

# if underlying data changes (no longer lngs_utm) then this has to change

for(name in names(model.list)) {

  mod <- model.list[[name]]
  df <- lngs_utm
  
  # get model names
  mod_fam <- mod$family$family
  fam_label <- paste(mod_fam, collapse = "_")
  
  # extract residuals
  sims <- simulate(mod, nsim = 500, type = "mle-mvn")
  resid <- dharma_residuals(sims, mod, return_DHARMa = TRUE)
  
  # create dharma plots as ggplots
  p_qq <- as.grob(~DHARMa::plotQQunif(resid))
  p_res <- as.grob(~DHARMa::plotResiduals(resid))
  
  # combine residual plots
  dharma_plots <- wrap_plots(p_qq, p_res) +
    plot_annotation(title = paste(name, fam_label, "DHARMa Diagnostics"))
  
  # put plot in a list to look at
  residual.plots[[name]] <- dharma_plots
  
  # put the residuals in a df for spatial plotting
  df$resid <- resid$scaledResiduals
  residual.df[[name]] <- df
  
  # create spatial plot
  spatials <- ggplot(df) +
    geom_point(aes(X,Y, col = resid)) +
    labs(title = paste(name, fam_label, "Spatial residuals")) +
    scale_colour_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0.5) +
    facet_wrap(~sample_year) +
    coord_fixed() +
    theme_minimal()
  
  # put into list to look at
  spatial.plots[[name]] <- spatials
  


  print(name)
  residual.df[[name]] <- df
  
}
```

##cross validation
The fits of all the different distributions look fine. If you continue down the 
script we compare the partial effects of length by year at an average spatial location and median doy 248

However lets fint some cv models to see if we can definitely choose a model
```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
plan(multisession)

gaus_cv <- sdmTMB_cv(
  data = lngs_utm,
  corrected_length ~ 0 + s(scale_doy2) + as.factor(sample_year),
  mesh = mesh.lng, 
  time = "sample_year", 
  family = gaussian(),
  spatial = "on",
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  anisotropy = TRUE,
  k_folds = 6
)

logN_cv <- sdmTMB_cv(
  data = lngs_utm,
  corrected_length ~ 0 + s(scale_doy2) + as.factor(sample_year),
  mesh = mesh.lng, 
  time = "sample_year", 
  family = lognormal(link = "log"),
  spatial = "on",
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  anisotropy = TRUE,
  k_folds = 6
)

gamma_cv <- sdmTMB_cv(
  data = lngs_utm,
  corrected_length ~ 0 + s(scale_doy2) + as.factor(sample_year),
  mesh = mesh.lng, 
  time = "sample_year", 
  family = gengamma(link = "log"),
  spatial = "on",
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  anisotropy = TRUE, 
  k_folds = 6
)
```

Comparing outputs
```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
#1. compare the nge log likelihood - closer to 0 is better
gaus_cv$sum_loglik
logN_cv$sum_loglik 
gamma_cv$sum_loglik

#2. look at mean log likelihoods
mean_loglike_gaus <- gaus_cv$sum_loglik / nrow(gaus_cv$data) 
mean_loglike_logN <- logN_cv$sum_loglik / nrow(logN_cv$data)
mean_loglike_gamma <- gamma_cv$sum_loglik / nrow(gamma_cv$data)

#3. look at RMSE across entire dataset
sqrt(mean((gaus_cv$data$corrected_length - gaus_cv$data$cv_predicted)^2)) 
sqrt(mean((logN_cv$data$corrected_length - logN_cv$data$cv_predicted)^2)) 
sqrt(mean((gamma_cv$data$corrected_length - gamma_cv$data$cv_predicted)^2)) 

#4. RMSE by folds
rmse_gaus <- dplyr::group_by(gaus_cv$data, cv_fold) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    mae = mean(abs(corrected_length - cv_predicted)),
    rmse = sqrt(mean((corrected_length - cv_predicted)^2)))
rmse_logN <- dplyr::group_by(logN_cv$data, cv_fold) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    mae = mean(abs(corrected_length - cv_predicted)),
    rmse = sqrt(mean((corrected_length - cv_predicted)^2)))
rmse_gamma <- dplyr::group_by(gamma_cv$data, cv_fold) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    mae = mean(abs(corrected_length - cv_predicted)),
    rmse = sqrt(mean((corrected_length - cv_predicted)^2)))
# hmm look the same
ggplot() +
  geom_line(aes(x = cv_fold, rmse), data = rmse_gaus, col = "red") +
  geom_line(aes(x = cv_fold, rmse), data = rmse_logN, col = "blue") +
  geom_line(aes(x = cv_fold, rmse), data = rmse_gamma, col = "green")

#' honestly hard to come up with a determination based on this, but the cross validation didn't seem to work super well with 
#' the gaussian distribution, the model doesn't convert with the different folds
#' the gamma seems to consistently have higher rmse so I t hink we'll split the diff and use the logN
```


create prediction
```{r}
# create prediction grid
## create sf object
lng_sf <- lngs_utm %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(c(X, Y, eq_latitude, eq_longitude)) %>%
  mutate(X = X*1000, Y = Y*1000) %>% # convert to meters for crs 32602
  st_as_sf(coords = c("X", "Y"), crs = 32602)

## create convex hull
convex <- concaveman(lng_sf, concavity = 3)

## add buffer to edges
convex_buff <- st_buffer(convex, dist = 15e3) # dist in meters (we think)
plot(convex_buff) # looks about right

## make grid
# make grid, created a cell size of 10,000 x 10,000 m (10 x 10 km) with poitns in center
# need to check units on this... 
grid <- st_make_grid(convex_buff, cellsize = 10e3, what = "centers") %>%
  st_intersection(convex_buff)

## change back to df
bs.grid <- do.call(rbind, st_geometry(grid)) %>%
  as_tibble() %>% setNames(c("X", "Y")) %>%
  # convert df m back to km
  mutate(X = X/1e3, Y = Y/1e3)
plot(bs.grid)

## replicate df across years and include any other variables we inlcude in our fit of the model
## i.e., depth tmeperature etc
scaled_median <- unique(lngs_utm$scaled_median)

bs.grid.year <- replicate_df(bs.grid, "sample_year", unique(lngs_utm$sample_year))
bs.grid.year.doy <- replicate_df(bs.grid.year, "scale_doy2", scaled_median) # this is at doy 248
```

predict back to observations

## index comparison

```{r}
# predict 
pred.gaus <- predict(fit.gaus, newdata = bs.grid.year.doy, return_tmb_object = T, type = "response")
pred.logN <- predict(fit.logN, newdata = bs.grid.year.doy, return_tmb_object = T, type = "response")
pred.gamma <- predict(fit.gamma, newdata = bs.grid.year.doy, return_tmb_object = T, type = "response")

# index
index.gaus <- get_index(pred.gaus, bias_correct = T)
index.logN <- get_index(pred.logN, bias_correct = T)
index.gamma <- get_index(pred.gamma, bias_correct = T)

# plot index and see how much they vary between distributions
ggplot() +
  geom_pointrange(data = index.gaus, aes(x = sample_year, y = est, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), color = "blue") +
  geom_pointrange(data = index.logN, aes(x = sample_year+0.1, y = est, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), color = "green") +
  geom_pointrange(data = index.gamma, aes(x = sample_year+0.5, y = est, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), color = "orange")
# the pattern is identical, the ci appears to be close (although some variation)
# the point estimates for gaussian are the lowest with logN slightly higher and gamma above that. 

library(ggeffects)
# marginal effect of sample_year holding DOY at median
eff.gaus <- ggpredict(fit.gaus, terms = "sample_year [all]")
eff.logN <- ggpredict(fit.logN, terms = "sample_year [all]")
eff.gamma <- ggpredict(fit.gamma, terms = "sample_year [all]")

eff.logN <- as.data.frame(eff.logN) %>%
  mutate(dist = "logN")
eff.gamma <- as.data.frame(eff.gamma) %>%
  mutate(dist = "gamma")

all.dat <- as.data.frame(eff.gaus) %>%
  mutate(dist = "gaussian") %>%
  rbind(eff.logN) %>%
  rbind(eff.gamma)

ggplot(all.dat) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(x= x, y = predicted, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high, color = dist), position = position_jitter()) +
  labs(x = "Years", y = "Predicted length (mm)")

ggplot(eff.logN) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(x= x, y = predicted, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high)) +
  labs(x = "Years", y = "Predicted length (mm)") +
  theme_minimal()

```

# Predicted mapping

## deviations from average
```{r}
# have to predict the correct model again but not keep the tmb object
pred <- predict(fit.logN, newdata = bs.grid.year.doy)

# create a sf of the predictions
pred.lng.sf <- pred %>%
  mutate(Y = Y*1000,
         X = X*1000) %>% # sf requires meters
  st_as_sf(coords = c("X", "Y"), crs = 32602) %>%
  st_transform(., crs = 4326) %>%
  st_shift_longitude()
  
# what might be helpful here too is the average spatial field 
#' by keeping the exp(omega) were showing the relative length anomaly across space. 
#' here (I think) it means that 1 is the average or baseline value (aka average length of a fish after accounting for doy & ran eff maybe)
#' the larger and smaller deviations are above and below 1. So 1.075 representes a fish that is 7.5% larger than the average
#' math: percent increase = exp(value) -1 * 100
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = bs_cropped_wgs, fill = "gray", color = "black", inherit.aes = F) +
  geom_sf(mapping = aes(fill = exp(omega_s), color = exp(omega_s)),
          data = pred.lng.sf, pch = 22) +
  geom_contour(data = bathline, aes(x = x +360, y = y, z = z),
               breaks = c(-20, -50, -100, -150), linewidth = 0.3, colour = "black") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")

#' if we wanted to know what the absolute length deviations from a fish you'd need to incorporate the average length of a fish
mean(exp(pred$est)) # I dunno if this is legit but for now lets call an average fish is 57 mm long
pred.lng.sf$absolute_omega_s <- (exp(pred.lng.sf$omega_s) - 1) * (mean(exp(pred$est)))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = bs_cropped_wgs, fill = "gray", color = "black", inherit.aes = F) +
  geom_sf(mapping = aes(fill = absolute_omega_s, color = absolute_omega_s),
          data = pred.lng.sf, pch = 22) +
  geom_contour(data = bathline, aes(x = x +360, y = y, z = z),
               breaks = c(-20, -50, -100, -150), linewidth = 0.3, colour = "black") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude", color = expression("Deviation from \naverage length (mm)"),
       fill = expression("Deviation from \naverage length (mm)"))
```

# Env models
Okay and close to the those particular length sdmTMB models. 
What does it look like to add in additional parameters to the model formula? 

Starting with the simple ones, temperature/coldpoolindex
```{r}
head(lngs_utm)
head(cold_pool_index)
cpi <- rename_with(cold_pool_index, tolower)

lngs_env <- lngs_utm %>%
  left_join(cpi, by = c("sample_year" = "year")) %>%
  mutate(sc_surf_tmp = scale(mean_surface_temperature),
         sample_year = as.numeric(sample_year)) 
```


```{r}
#' what do we think we're fitting here? 
#' looking at the spatial/spatiotemporal patterns in length of pollock when accounting for yearly
#' variability in surface temperature and doy
fit.stmp <- sdmTMB(
  data = lngs_env,
  corrected_length ~ scale_doy2 + s(mean_surface_temperature, k = 4),
  mesh = mesh.lng, 
  time = "sample_year", 
  family = lognormal(link = "log"),
  spatial = "off",
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  anisotropy = TRUE
)

sanity(fit.stmp)
tidy(fit.stmp, "ran_pars")
tidy(fit.stmp)
check_gradient(fit.stmp)
```

### model eval
```{r}
mod <- fit.stmp 
df <- lngs_env
  # extract residuals
  sims <- simulate(mod, nsim = 500, type = "mle-mvn")
  resid <- dharma_residuals(sims, mod, return_DHARMa = TRUE)
  
  # create dharma plots as ggplots
  p_qq <- as.grob(~DHARMa::plotQQunif(resid))
  p_res <- as.grob(~DHARMa::plotResiduals(resid))
  
  # combine residual plots
  dharma_plots <- wrap_plots(p_qq, p_res) +
    plot_annotation(title = paste(name, fam_label, "DHARMa Diagnostics"))
  
  # view
  dharma_plots
  
  # put the residuals in a df for spatial plotting
  df$resid <- resid$scaledResiduals
  
  # create spatial plot
  spatials <- ggplot(df) +
    geom_point(aes(X,Y, col = resid)) +
    labs(title =  "Spatial residuals") +
    scale_colour_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0.5) +
    facet_wrap(~sample_year) +
    coord_fixed() +
    theme_minimal()

  # view 
  spatials
```


## predict

                     condition = c(scale_doy2 = scaled_median,
